dedupe_keys.name: pytseb two source energy balance models

description: pyTSEB is Nieto, Guzinski, Kustas and contributors' Python implementation of two-source energy-balance models for estimating evapotranspiration. It includes Priestley-Taylor TSEB, dual-time-difference and separate soil/canopy-temperature formulations, with point-series and image workflows. Inputs are radiometric surface temperatures, meteorological conditions and canopy parameters; outputs are sensible and latent heat fluxes and related water-energy exchanges. Spatial and temporal coverage follow the supplied imagery or observations. Source is free under GPL-3.0 and provides configuration examples and notebooks. A limitation is that wrongly specified measurement heights, canopy clumping or green fractions can produce erroneous results; the authors also recognise limitations under some conditions even with appropriate inputs. pyTSEB can estimate water-demand and land-surface terms for irrigation and infrastructure adaptation simulations. pylandtemp (platform-pylandtemp) offers related temperature retrieval. No remote-sensing data or model environment was downloaded.
